q: A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor.
e: True. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows. A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor.

q: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by a conductor.
e: False. The right claim is this: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other insulating material. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The printed line wrongly says a parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by a conductor.

q: The surface charge density $\sigma$ on each plate is expressed as $\sigma = \frac{A}{Q}$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The surface charge density (charge per unit surface area) on each plate is expressed as sigma = Q/A. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. The printed line wrongly says the surface charge density sigma on each plate is expressed as sigma = (A)/(Q).

q: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is uniform.
e: True. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Are very close together, the electric field between the plates is uniform.

q: The value of the electric field between the plates can be expressed as $E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}$.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The relation in this line is E = (sigma)/(ε).

q: The electric field between the plates is expressed as $E = \frac{Q}{\varepsilon A}$.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The relation in this line is E = (Q)/(ε A).

q: Because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals $E / d$.
e: False. The right claim is this: Because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals Ed. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. The printed line wrongly says because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals E / d.

q: The potential difference V between the plates is given by $V = \frac{Qd}{\varepsilon A}$.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The relation in this line is V = (Qd)/(ε A).

q: The capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor is $C = \frac{\varepsilon A}{d}$.
e: True. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. The relation in this line is C = (ε A)/(d).

q: For a given insulating material, the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the area of its plates.
e: False. The right claim is this: For a given insulating material the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the area of its plates. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. The printed line wrongly says for a given insulating material, the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the area of its plates.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the separation of the plates.
e: True. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows. A parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the separation of the plates.

q: The permittivity $\varepsilon$ of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum $\varepsilon_0$ as $\varepsilon = \frac{K}{\varepsilon_0}$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The permittivity ε of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum ε0 as ε = Kε0. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The printed line wrongly says the permittivity ε of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum ε0 as ε = (K)/(ε0).

q: K is the dielectric constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. K is the dielectric constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material.

q: For a vacuum, the dielectric constant K is equal to 0.
e: False. The right claim is this: For a vacuum, the dielectric constant K is 1. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum. The printed line wrongly says for a vacuum, the dielectric constant K is equal to 0.

q: For insulating materials other than vacuum, the dielectric constant K is greater than 1.
e: True. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. For insulating materials other than vacuum, the dielectric constant K is greater than 1.

q: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. Insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum.

q: The dielectric constant K can be expressed as $K = \frac{\varepsilon_0}{\varepsilon}$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The permittivity of vacuum ε0 can also be expressed in the unit A s^-1. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The printed line wrongly says the dielectric constant K can be expressed as K = (ε0)/(ε).

q: The dielectric constant is defined as the ratio of the capacitance of a capacitor with an insulating material to the capacitance of that capacitor with a vacuum.
e: True. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. An insulating material to the capacitance of that capacitor with a vacuum.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the charge Q of the capacitor increases.
e: False. The right claim is this: When a charged capacitor is disconnected and a dielectric is inserted, the capacitance of the capacitor increases. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. The printed line wrongly says when a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the charge Q of the capacitor increases.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference of the capacitor is found to decrease.
e: True. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. Is inserted, the potential difference of the capacitor is found to decrease.

q: Since the potential difference decreases when a dielectric is inserted into a disconnected charged capacitor, the capacitance of the capacitor increases.
e: True. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Inserted into a disconnected charged capacitor, the capacitance of the capacitor increases.

q: The dielectric constant K can be expressed as the ratio of potential differences $K = \frac{V}{V_0}$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The dielectric constant K can be defined as the ratio of the capacitance with an insulator to the capacitance with a vacuum. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum. The printed line wrongly says the dielectric constant K can be expressed as the ratio of potential differences K = (V)/(V0).

q: Insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K less than unity.
e: False. The right claim is this: Insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K greater than unity. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum. The printed line wrongly says insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K less than unity.

q: A dielectric provides an increase in capacitance.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. A dielectric provides an increase in capacitance.

q: A dielectric decreases the maximum operating voltage of a capacitor.
e: False. The right claim is this: A dielectric increases the maximum operating voltage of a capacitor even though the physical size doesn't change. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. The printed line wrongly says a dielectric decreases the maximum operating voltage of a capacitor.

q: A dielectric provides possible mechanical support between the plates.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. A dielectric provides possible mechanical support between the plates.

q: Mechanical support from a dielectric allows the plates to be close together without electrical contact.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. A dielectric allows the plates to be close together without electrical contact.

q: Decreasing the separation d between plates decreases the capacitance C.
e: False. The right claim is this: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the separation of the plates. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. The printed line wrongly says decreasing the separation d between plates decreases the capacitance C.

q: A dielectric increases the maximum operating voltage of a capacitor even though the physical size of the capacitor doesn't change.
e: True. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. A capacitor even though the physical size of the capacitor doesn't change.

q: The dielectric may be able to withstand a smaller electric field between the plates than air.
e: False. The right claim is this: The dielectric may be able to withstand a larger electric field between the plates than air. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. The printed line wrongly says the dielectric may be able to withstand a smaller electric field between the plates than air.

q: The permittivity of vacuum $\varepsilon_0$ is $8.85 \times 10^{-12}$ C$^2$ N$^{-1}$ m$^{-2}$.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The power 10^-12 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.

q: The unit of permittivity of vacuum can also be written as F m$^{-1}$.
e: True. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The unit of permittivity of vacuum can also be written as F m^-1.

q: The dielectric constant of water at 18°C is 1.
e: False. The right claim is this: According to Table 9. 1, the dielectric constant of Water (18°C) is 81. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum.

q: The dielectric constant of air at 1 atm is 1.0006.
e: True. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum. The dielectric constant of air at 1 atm is 1.0006.
